- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope afterward.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model forecast is trending upward, check for mean reversion; if price has been rising for 5+ days, cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent high.
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating 0.3–0.7), model often overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before major moves.
- If true outcome is consistently below model forecast (especially in 30d horizon), model may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is rising (e.g., 0.6+ over 3+ days) and model is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum; increase forecast by 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
- For 30d forecasts, if last 5 days’ true values are trending downward, model often fails to anticipate reversal; add a slight upward bias (1–3%) to counteract mean reversion bias.
